title: upgradescope JSON report, schemaVersion 1
description: What `upgradescope scan --output json` and `--write-baseline` write. Within schemaVersion 1 fields are only added, never renamed, removed, retyped or given a new meaning, so the schema allows unknown fields: ignore them. Finding categories may be added too, so `category` is an open string; severity, verdict and baselineState values are fixed. internal/cli/docs_test.go validates real scan output against this file and fails on a field it does not list.

toolVersion.description: The binary that wrote the report. Informational, no compatibility meaning.

filesBase.description: --files only: the scanned directory, which object file paths are relative to. Slash-separated and relative to the working directory when it is inside it ("" = the working directory), absolute otherwise.

clusterId.description: The kube-system namespace UID, or "files" for a --files scan.

serverVersion.description: Live scans: the kube-apiserver's raw gitVersion (e.g. v1.34.2-gke.100), the version the target was judged against. Absent in --files mode.

kubeContext.description: Live scans: the kubeconfig context the scan read. Absent in --files mode.

apiServer.description: Live scans: the API server the scan read, as scheme, host and port (e.g. https://10.0.0.1:6443); never the kubeconfig's credentials, path or query. Absent in --files mode.

kbVersion.description: The knowledge base the report was judged with.

score.description: max(0, 100 - min(75, 25 x blockers) - min(20, 5 x warnings)); suppressed findings excluded.

ready.description: verdict == ready. Kept for v0.1 readers; prefer verdict.

verdict.description: blocked: a blocker. unknown: no blocker, but a required check was not assessed. ready: neither.

unrecognizedImages.description: Image repositories (host/path, no tag) that no add-on image matcher recognised: a gap in add-on detection, not a finding, so they change neither score nor verdict. An add-on running one is still found through its pod labels, IngressClass or Helm release. Sorted, deduplicated, at most 200.

unrecognizedImagesOmitted.description: Unrecognized image repositories beyond the 200 listed.

addOnEvidenceAgeSeconds.description: How old, in seconds (at least 1), the pod evidence the add-ons were detected from was when the agent reused its last full pod pass instead of listing every pod again (--pod-pass-every, --pod-pass-max-age): an add-on installed or upgraded since is reported as it was then, for at most the agent's --pod-pass-max-age. Absent when every pod was read for this report, and from collectors that predate the field. The verdict does not depend on it.

hops.description: scan --plan only: the upgrade plan, one entry per control-plane upgrade from the cluster's minor (a live scan's oldest kube-apiserver, or --from) to target, in order. Each finding is listed in full at the first hop that has it and referenced by key at later ones. The rest of the report, the verdict included, is the final target's.

teams.description: Per-team scores; findings with no team are under "(unattributed)". Present when there are findings.

support.description: Live scans of a cluster on EKS, GKE or AKS whose Kubernetes minor the knowledge base dates: where that minor stands in the provider's support calendar, whether or not it is a finding. Absent for other clusters, for manifests, and when the provider's dates for the minor are not known. The same for every target. See the `support-lifecycle` finding.

provider.description: The managed Kubernetes service the collector inferred from the server version suffix and the nodes' managed node pool labels.

phase.description: standard: standard support, not ending within 90 days. ending: standard support ends within 90 days. extended: past standard support, before the provider's extended window ends (EKS bills it by default; on GKE and AKS it is opt-in, see `extendedSupportCondition`, and the cluster may not be enrolled). ended: past the end of extended support, or past standard support for a minor with no extended support.

extendedSupportFrom.description: The day (UTC) standard support ends and extended support begins. EKS bills extended support from the start of this day.

extendedSupportEnds.description: The day extended support ends; absent when the provider offered none for the minor.

annualCostDelta.description: What extended support adds per cluster per year at the provider's published list price, (extended - standard) x 8760 cluster-hours, as a decimal string in `currency`. A list price as of `priceAsOf`, not the customer's bill: prices change and vary by contract. Present only when the knowledge base cites the provider's price and the minor can still be in extended support (not in phase `ended`); never inferred.

priceAsOf.description: The day the list price behind `annualCostDelta` was read from the provider's pricing page.

annualCostNote.description: The provider's caveat on whom `annualCostDelta` is charged to (GKE: only clusters on the Extended release channel). Present with `annualCostDelta` when the knowledge base records one; show it beside the figure.

extendedSupportCondition.description: Where the provider's extended support is opt-in (GKE, AKS): the configuration under which it applies, as a clause completing "only if ..." ("Long Term Support is enabled"). The scanner cannot see the cluster's configuration, so phases `ending` and `extended` describe the provider's window, not a confirmed enrolment. Absent for EKS and when the provider offered no extended support for the minor.

category.description: One of `removed-api`, `deprecated-api`, `deprecated-api-in-use`, `eol-addon`, `eol-approaching`, `version-skew`, `chart-incompat`, `kb-stale`, `addon-no-data`, `unknown-api`, `crd-version`, `support-lifecycle`. A release may add categories within schemaVersion 1, so this is not an enum: treat one you do not know by its severity.

key.description: Stable, count-free identity: category/discriminator. Baselines and notifications match on it.

unnamespaced.description: An add-on finding that also covers an install in no named namespace: a manifest object without metadata.namespace, or a cluster-scoped IngressClass. A namespace-scoped ignore rule cannot be shown to match it, so it does not take the finding.

baselineState.description: With --baseline: unchanged (the baseline had it) or new.

callers.description: API usage findings: the apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis rows folded into this finding, in row order, each the deprecated-api-in-use finding it is on its own. Suppressing every object of the finding by annotation or an object-scoped rule does not suppress them: they then stand as findings of their own.

key.description: The key of the caller's own deprecated-api-in-use finding.

source.description: What suppressed it: the config file, annotation, or spec.ignore.

expires.description: YYYY-MM-DD, as the rule gave it.

file.description: Manifest path, slash-separated, relative to filesBase.

line.description: 1-based line of the object's apiVersion key.

renderedFrom.description: The Helm template the object was rendered from (# Source: comment).

manager.description: Live objects: the field manager that wrote it through the flagged API, or kubectl last-applied.

required.description: The gap makes the verdict unknown.

to.description: The minor the control plane reaches at this hop; the cluster as it is, judged at it.

score.description: The score at this hop's to.

verdict.description: The verdict at this hop's to, counting new and referenced findings.

findings.description: Findings first seen at this hop, in full.

changed.description: Findings listed at an earlier hop whose severity differs from the last earlier hop that had them.

carried.description: Findings listed at an earlier hop, at the same severity.

notAssessed.description: Every gap at this hop's to.

was.description: changed only: the severity at the last earlier hop that had the finding.

since.description: The to of the hop that lists the finding in full.

verdict.description: The team's readiness, by the report's rules over what can concern it: blocked by a blocker of its own or by an unattributed one (which cannot be ruled out as the team's); otherwise unknown when the report has a required not-assessed gap, which may hide any team's blocker; otherwise ready. Another team's blocker does not lower it; score, blockers and warnings count only the team's own findings.
